title: Voice form: collect spoken answers as structured fields
description: A practical guide to voice forms: what they are, when spoken answers help, how review and text fallback work, and how to try one safely in your browser.
eyebrow: Voice input with a reviewable result
definition: A voice form lets someone answer form questions by speaking instead of typing every response. A useful implementation does more than save a transcript: it maps each answer to an expected field, asks for missing details, and gives the respondent a chance to review or correct the result. Talkform keeps the public demo in the browser and offers an equivalent text path when voice is unavailable or unwanted.
bestFor: Open-ended feedback where the reason matters as much as the rating
Intake that asks for goals, constraints, or a recent example
Mobile situations where a long typed answer creates avoidable effort
workflow: Define only the fields the receiving workflow actually needs
Explain why voice is offered and keep text available as an equal option
Ask one clear question at a time and clarify only missing fields
Let the respondent review structured values before export or submission
tradeoffs: Voice is not appropriate in every environment, so text fallback is essential
Transcription and extraction can be wrong; respondents need field-level correction
A voice form does not by itself improve completion or make a sample representative

questions.question: What is a voice form?
questions.answer: It is a form experience that accepts spoken answers and maps them into defined, reviewable fields instead of treating the recording or transcript as the final result.

questions.question: Can respondents type instead?
questions.answer: They should be able to. Talkform's demo supports a text interview path, and a production implementation should not require microphone access when text can collect the same information.

questions.question: Where does the public demo store answers?
questions.answer: The public demo keeps transcript, summary, and answer state in the respondent's browser until they choose to export. Do not place answer text in analytics events.

title: Conversational forms: a field-by-field guide
description: Learn how conversational forms turn a fixed schema into a guided voice or text interview, when follow-up questions help, and where ordinary forms remain better.
eyebrow: A conversation backed by a schema
definition: Conversational forms present a form as a sequence of natural questions while still producing the named fields a downstream system expects. The conversation can acknowledge an answer, clarify a missing date or choice, and then show the structured record for review. The form schema remains the source of truth; the assistant should not invent fields, make eligibility decisions, or silently submit an answer the respondent has not checked.
bestFor: Lead or project intake that mixes fixed choices with open-ended context
Customer onboarding where goals and constraints need clarification
Research screeners that benefit from a consistent question sequence
workflow: Start from the destination schema and remove fields that are not needed
Write neutral prompts that make the purpose and expected effort clear
Use follow-ups only to complete or disambiguate a defined field
Review the resulting record before a human uses or exports it
tradeoffs: A conversation can take longer than a short form with familiar fields
Adaptive follow-ups require careful testing so the interview stays in scope
Consequential routing and qualification still require transparent rules and human review

questions.question: How is a conversational form different from a chatbot?
questions.answer: A conversational form is bounded by a known set of fields and a defined completion state. An open chatbot can range across topics without producing a complete, validated form record.

questions.question: Does it have to use voice?
questions.answer: No. A conversational form can run in text, voice, or offer both. The important distinction is guided field collection with review, not the input modality.

questions.question: Can it qualify leads automatically?
questions.answer: It can collect consistent qualification inputs, but Talkform should not make unreviewed eligibility decisions. Route the reviewed export to a person or a separately governed rules process.

title: Chat form: guided text intake without a blank message box
description: See how a chat form differs from live chat and traditional forms, how to keep it bounded to a schema, and how to test a text-first interview in Talkform.
eyebrow: Text conversation with a defined finish line
definition: A chat form collects a known set of fields through a message-style interface. Unlike general live chat, it has an explicit purpose, required fields, validation rules, and a review step. Unlike a static form, it can present one question at a time and ask a narrow follow-up when an answer is incomplete. Talkform's text mode demonstrates this pattern without requiring microphone permission or pretending an unbounded support agent is present.
bestFor: Onboarding flows where one-question-at-a-time pacing reduces cognitive load
Structured intake that needs a short clarification before moving on
Respondents who prefer text but benefit from a guided sequence
workflow: State the purpose, field count, and what happens to the completed record
Present one question with a visible way to skip optional fields
Validate the field without discarding the respondent's prior work
Show all captured values for correction before export or submission
tradeoffs: One-question-at-a-time flows can hide overall length unless progress is visible
A chat presentation should not imply a human is responding when it is automated
For names, dates, and short choices, a conventional field may remain faster

questions.question: What is a chat form?
questions.answer: It is a structured form presented as a text conversation, with defined fields, validation, progress, and a completion state.

questions.question: Is a chat form the same as live chat?
questions.answer: No. Live chat is usually an open support or sales conversation. A chat form is bounded intake and should make its automated behavior and expected output clear.

questions.question: Can a chat form also offer voice?
questions.answer: Yes, provided text remains fully usable. Talkform models voice and text as two paths to the same reviewable fields rather than separate data formats.

title: Voice survey: capture a score and the story behind it
description: Plan a voice survey that combines ratings with open-ended context, keeps consent and text fallback clear, and returns answers people can review before export.
definition: A voice survey lets a respondent speak some or all of a survey response while preserving structured questions such as ratings, choices, and follow-up consent. It is most useful when an open-ended explanation would be burdensome to type. A responsible design still shows the survey purpose, provides text input, confirms extracted fields, and treats the resulting comments as personal data rather than harmless analytics metadata.
bestFor: NPS or satisfaction surveys that need the reason behind a score
Post-project feedback where respondents can describe one concrete example
Short research follow-ups that combine ratings and qualitative context
workflow: Keep the rating question and scale explicit rather than inferring sentiment
Invite one focused spoken explanation after the structured response
Ask separately for follow-up permission and a safe contact method
Review scores, extracted fields, and comments before analysis or routing
tradeoffs: A voice option does not correct sampling bias or guarantee more responses
Do not infer emotion, demographics, or customer value from vocal characteristics
Long recordings increase privacy, review, and retention responsibilities

questions.question: Can a voice survey include ratings?
questions.answer: Yes. Keep the scale visible and explicit, then use voice or text for the explanation. Do not infer a rating from tone of voice.

questions.question: Should every survey question accept a long spoken answer?
questions.answer: Usually not. Use voice where context is valuable and keep simple choices simple. Removing unnecessary questions is often more useful than changing their modality.

questions.question: How should voice survey data be analyzed?
questions.answer: Analyze reviewed fields and comments with the same privacy controls used for other survey data. Keep transcripts and personal answers out of ordinary product analytics.
